correctness.rationale: For white support in at least two parts the white-induced graph is connected, and a blue vertex in part \(A_i\) has exactly \(|W|-w_i\) white neighbors. Therefore a PSD force exists exactly in the stated two-part singleton-side configuration; after that force all remaining whites occupy one independent part and are forced component by component. The disjoint white-support count gives the polynomial. Independent exhaustive simulation through order 10 returned VERIFY_OK with 64,916 subset checks and 1,179 coefficient checks.

originality.rationale: The directly relevant prior theorem of Peters determines only the scalar complete-multipartite PSD zero forcing number. The retained claim is the stronger all-set structural characterization and exact size-generating polynomial. Searches under PSD/positive-semidefinite terminology, complete multipartite/bipartite aliases, and polynomial/enumerator language did not locate this stronger coverage.
residual_risks: Poorly indexed or non-digitized work may contain an equivalent all-set classification without using polynomial/enumerator terminology.
The 2012 complete-multipartite scalar theorem is decisive prior coverage for the minimum value, so no originality is claimed for \(Z_+(G)=N-\max_i n_i\) itself.

value.rationale: PSD zero forcing is a classical graph parameter motivated by positive semidefinite minimum rank. A complete feasible-set classification and full size enumerator refine a known scalar family result in a mathematically natural way, reveal the exact component-rule mechanism, and support subsequent counting, reliability, or random-initialization questions without requiring re-simulation.
